risks.note: The Company aims to scale production to four million units annually by FY 2030-31, nearly double its current capacity. It took almost 40 years to reach two million units; the next two million is to be added in just 7-8 years, a pace nearly five times faster. This requires significantly more human capital, financial investment and technical know-how plus faster decision-making, and stakeholder partners - suppliers, dealers and transporters - must scale in tandem.
risks.risk: Risks associated with the increased scale of operations

risks.note: With nearly 450 Tier-1 and about 1,500 Tier-2 suppliers, supply disruption remains a major business continuity risk. Export restrictions on certain critical materials during the year highlighted the vulnerability of globally concentrated supply chains, and geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and logistics disruptions may continue to affect supply availability. Mitigation is localisation, alternate sources, diversified sourcing locations and the Vendor Comprehensive Excellence Programme.
risks.risk: Continuity of component supplies across a concentrated supplier base

risks.note: Increasing adoption of advanced automotive technologies raises dependence on specialised materials and critical components whose supply chains remain concentrated in a few countries; in an increasingly dynamic geopolitical environment, material-availability risk is likely to persist. In the near term, geopolitical tensions in West Asia may exert pressure on profitability through higher commodity prices.
risks.risk: Dependence on specialised materials and critical components sourced from a limited number of countries

risks.note: Electrification, software-defined vehicles, advanced electronics and connectivity are transforming the industry, but several of these technologies are yet to reach the cost competitiveness needed for widespread adoption in a price-sensitive market such as India. As the BEV, SHEV and advanced-feature portfolio expands, holding cost competitiveness while preserving affordability is a key strategic priority, addressed through localisation, value engineering and supplier base expansion.
risks.risk: Cost competitiveness of emerging and advanced technologies in a price-sensitive market

risks.note: Sudden and significant increases in the prices of metals, energy and other commodities can adversely impact profitability and business performance, a risk reinforced by recent geopolitical developments. This risk materialised in FY 2025-26: operating margin moderated to 8.4% from 10.0%, driven by adverse commodity prices and supply-side pressures, with the Company choosing not to pass on the full cost increases. Mitigation includes consumption optimisation, alternate materials, material circularity, hedging, forward contracts and long-term commercial arrangements.

Scaling operations amid rapid technological transformation increases demand for new skillsets both internally and across value chain partners; at the same time, sustaining the organisational values, culture of partnership and continuous-improvement spirit built over four decades becomes harder as scale and workforce expand.
risks.risk: Capacity and capability for future readiness - skills, leadership pipeline and cultural continuity at scale

risks.note: Cyber threats are growing and the Company protects information assets through employee education on phishing and proactive monitoring. It has created a cybersecurity assessment framework based on global standards for suppliers, and over 400 Tier-1 supplier partners have been assessed so far, on the view that supply-chain cyber resilience is a business-continuity issue.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity, including cyber risk in the supply chain

risks.note: The Company is exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, mainly on the import of components, raw materials and services and on the export of vehicles and services. It runs a structured exchange risk management policy and uses hedge instruments judiciously depending on market conditions and the currency view. The MD&A separately records a sharp depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar towards the end of the year.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports
